headline: State Leaders Agree To Attend Joint Event Only If Seating Is Arranged In A Perfect Non-Euclidean Geometric Shape
body:
Following a highly publicized effort to set aside ego for the sake of party unity, regional political leaders have announced a breakthrough: they will appear together at a public rally, provided the event organizers arrange their chairs in a non-Euclidean configuration that ensures neither leader is technically 'in front of' or 'behind' the other.

“The geometry is quite complex,” explained Ramanujan Rao, a structural consultant hired by the party high command to mediate the seating chart. “We have calculated that by placing the chairs on a curved fold of spacetime, we can ensure that both leaders are effectively occupying the same prime position relative to the podium, without either one perceiving the other as having a superior vantage point. It’s basic quantum political alignment.”

To further assist in the peace process, the stage will feature a rotating dais that completes one full revolution every three seconds, ensuring that no leader can be associated with a specific side of the room. The local party office has also requested that all photographers use wide-angle lenses to ensure both individuals occupy exactly 50 percent of the frame at all times, with a software-generated watermark of a white dove hovering precisely in the center of the image.

“I am fully committed to our shared future, as long as my chair is bolted to a levitating platform that remains perfectly equidistant from the exit, the snacks, and my counterpart’s periphery,” noted a senior party strategist speaking on condition of anonymity. “If the chairs are off by even a millimeter, we have a contingency plan involving a holographic projection of both leaders that doesn't actually require either of them to be in the same city.”
caption: Physics meets politics as regional leaders prepare for a joint event using advanced geometric seating to maintain perfect ego-equilibrium. 🪑📐 #PoliticalGeometry #UnityInSpace #StatePolitics (satire)
igHook: Would you go to such lengths to avoid sitting next to someone you don't like?
imagePrompt: A wide shot of a modern, empty political stage featuring two identical chairs placed at an awkward, steep angle on a circular platform in a large conference hall.

sourceHeadline.title: Konda And Revanth Set Egos Aside For Party Unity!

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 uses the most imaginative and absurd premise—non-Euclidean geometry to solve political ego—while maintaining a perfectly straight, bureaucratic tone. It avoids the repetitive 'shared object/separate room' trope found in almost every other submission, providing a fresher and more vivid image.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional premise about political ego to create a satirical piece. The named consultant is a generic fictional name, no real individuals are identified, and the content is whimsical and harmless.
